message.content:
Below are two ways to launch a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU** and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> ⚠️ **Prerequisites**
>
> * You must have the **Compute Engine API** enabled for your project.
> * Your account must have the `roles/compute.admin` role (or equivalent).
> * The **GPU quota** for your region must allow at least one RTX A6000.
> * The **NVIDIA GPU driver** can be installed automatically via a startup‑script (see below).

---

## 1️⃣ gcloud CLI Command

```bash
# Variables – replace with your own values
PROJECT_ID="your-gcp-project-id"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
ZONE="us-central1-b"          # choose a zone that supports RTX A6000
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"  # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM – adjust if needed
DISK_SIZE_GB="100"            # boot disk size
DISK_TYPE="pd-balanced"       # persistent disk type

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
    --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
    --zone="$ZONE" \
    --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size="${DISK_SIZE_GB}GB" \
    --boot-disk-type="$DISK_TYPE" \
    --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
    --tags http-server,https-server
```

### `startup.sh` – Install NVIDIA Drivers Automatically

Create a file named `startup.sh` in the same directory:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Update package lists
apt-get update

# Install prerequisites
apt-get install -y build-essential dkms linux-headers-$(uname -r)

# Add NVIDIA package repositories
add-apt-repository ppa:graphics-drivers/ppa -y
apt-get update

# Install the latest NVIDIA driver (will match the GPU)
apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535

# Reboot to activate the driver
reboot
```

> **Tip:** If you prefer to use the **NVIDIA GPU Driver Installer** provided by GCP, replace the above script with:
> ```bash
> #!/bin/bash
> curl -O https://dl.google.com/linux/direct/nvidia-driver-installer-535.54.03.run
> chmod +x nvidia-driver-installer-535.54.03.run
> ./nvidia-driver-installer-535.54.03.run
> reboot
> ```

---

## 2️⃣ REST API Call (JSON Body)

If you prefer to use the **Compute Engine REST API**, here’s a minimal JSON payload you can POST to `https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances`.

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/us-central1-b/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/us-central1-b/diskTypes/pd-balanced"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/us-central1-b/types/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y build-essential dkms linux-headers-$(uname -r)\nadd-apt-repository ppa:graphics-drivers/ppa -y\napt-get update\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535\nreboot"
      }
    ]
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
```

> Replace `{PROJECT_ID}` and `{ZONE}` with your actual project ID and zone.  
> Use the **Google Cloud SDK** (`gcloud auth application-default login`) or OAuth 2.0 to authenticate the request.

---

### Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|---|------|
| ✅ | Compute Engine API enabled |
| ✅ | GPU quota available for RTX A6000 |
| ✅ | Correct machine type (e.g., `n1-standard-8`) |
| ✅ | Proper image family (`ubuntu-2004-lts`) |
| ✅ | Accelerator type set to `nvidia-tesla-a6000` |
| ✅ | Startup script installs NVIDIA drivers |

Once the instance boots, you can SSH into it and verify the GPU:

```bash
ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu@<EXTERNAL_IP>
nvidia-smi
```

That should show the RTX A6000 GPU and its driver version. Happy computing!
